Before we get to the HILLS, comment START to learn step by step how you can create and sell digital products. NOW THE HILLS: 1. Your product doesn’t need more pages. It needs a reason for someone to buy it. A 10-page guide that solves a specific problem can be more useful than a 100-page ebook full of information they could Google. 2. Being good at Canva isn’t enough. I was a graphic designer. Making things pretty was my thing. But you also need to explain who your product is for and why they need it. 3. Creating another product won’t fix avoiding marketing. If nobody knows about the first one, making five more just gives you five more things nobody knows about. 😅 4. Before you list your first digital product for sale, put yourself in your customer's shoes. 🌸 Imagine finding a beautiful planner online. You love the design, but you can't tell what's included, whether you can edit it, or how you'll receive it. Would you feel confident buying? Here's what every beginner digital product seller should explain clearly: 🌷 1. WHO IS IT FOR? Don't just say “Digital Planner.” Try: “A weekly family planner designed for busy moms who want to organize meals, appointments, and household tasks.” 🤍 2. WHAT EXACTLY IS INCLUDED? Tell buyers the number of pages, file format, and whether the product is printable, editable, or both. Only promise features your product actually has. 🎀 3. HOW WILL THEY RECEIVE IT? Explain whether they'll receive a PDF download, an editable Canva template link, or another format. Make sure your delivery instructions are simple and accurate. ✨ Here's the lesson: Creating a beautiful product is only one part of selling digital products. Helping customers understand what they're buying is just as important. Before worrying about getting more views, make sure your product listing answers the questions a beginner buyer would naturally ask. Clarity builds confidence.
